public_rationale: His firm commitment is that OpenAI and Anthropic will both start charging customers more. He gave no deadline. The token-billing and subscription-cut parts are hedged as 'very likely' and are not required here. By 2026-10-28 both companies were on the IPO path: Anthropic had filed an S-1, and OpenAI's IPO was expected in early 2027. I found no confirmed rise in the price of an existing product at either company after the post. Anthropic paused a planned billing change in June 2026 and left subscription limits unchanged. Reports of a ChatGPT Plus rise could not be confirmed and conflict with most sources. Because there is no deadline, the absence of a rise so far is not failure. The forecast stays open.
limitations: Much of the pricing coverage after June 2026 comes from SEO-style blogs that contradict each other, and several primary pages could not be read.
Tighter usage limits at the same price, which happened at times, could reasonably be called charging more. This contract does not count them.

our_interpretation: The firm commitment is only that both companies will start charging customers more. The billing shift and the subscription cuts are marked 'very likely', so they are hedged. They are described in the commentary but are not required for support.
The IPO race is the stated reason, not a condition. Support does not require proof that the IPO caused any price rise.

Plain reading of 'charging more': each company raises the price customers pay for an existing paid product after the post. That means a higher list price for an existing subscription tier, or a higher per-token rate for the same model. A new, more expensive tier is not a rise for existing customers. criteria.support_condition: After 2026-06-08, both OpenAI and Anthropic each raise the price customers pay for an existing paid product, such as a subscription list price or a per-token rate for the same model.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With no deadline, no single event contradicts the forecast. It could only be judged false if one or both companies plainly never raised prices over a long period after reaching IPO. No such period has passed.
